title: Effectivity of proper-space families over square-zero inverse sequences
statement: Let $(R_n)_{n\geq1}$ be an inverse sequence of commutative rings with compatible transition maps $\rho_{mn}:R_m\to R_n$ for $m\geq n$, all surjective and satisfying $(\ker\rho_{mn})^2=0$. Let $R=\varprojlim_n R_n$, concretely the ring of compatible sequences with coordinatewise operations. For every $n$ let $X_n\to\operatorname{Spec}R_n$ be a flat proper finitely presented morphism of algebraic spaces. Suppose specified isomorphisms $X_m\times_{\operatorname{Spec}R_m}\operatorname{Spec}R_n\cong X_n$ for $m\geq n$ satisfy the identity and cocycle compatibilities. Spectra and base changes use [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-pc-fibre-product]. Algebraic spaces are as in [def-trf-algebraic-space], with universes as in [def-weil-size-convention]. Flatness and local finite presentation of their morphisms are tested on etale scheme charts using [def-weil-flat-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Finite presentation means quasi-compact, quasi-separated and locally of finite presentation; quasi-separated means that the diagonal is quasi-compact. Proper means separated, of finite type and universally closed: separated means the diagonal is a closed immersion, finite type means quasi-compact and locally of finite type on etale charts, and universally closed means closed on underlying spaces after every algebraic-space base change (the scheme conventions are [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]). Then there exists a flat proper finitely presented morphism of algebraic spaces $X\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ and isomorphisms $X\times_{\operatorname{Spec}R}\operatorname{Spec}R_n\cong X_n$ compatible with every specified transition isomorphism. There is no Noetherian hypothesis on the rings, and no dimension or projectivity hypothesis on the spaces.

source.place: Tag 0D3X (lemma-spaces-defo-thy), proof, paragraphs beginning Let (R_n) be an inverse system and Let I_n = Ker(R_n to R_1), through the final deform-property argument.

proof.text: Put $I_n=\ker(R_n\to R_1)$ and $I=\varprojlim I_n$. Each $I_n^2=0$. The maps $I_m\to I_n$ are surjective: a lift in $R_m$ of an element of $I_n$ still maps to zero in $R_1$. Recursively lifting along the adjacent surjections shows that every projection $R\to R_n$ and $I\to I_n$ is surjective. The kernel of $R\to R_1$ is exactly $I$, since this condition holds coordinatewise, and $I^2=0$ coordinatewise. Thus $0\to I\to R\to R_1\to0$ is a square-zero ring extension. No assertion that adjacent square-zero kernels alone imply $I_n^2=0$ is being used: the hypothesis applies to every $R_n\to R_1$.

source.place: Tag 0D3X (lemma-spaces-defo-thy), proof, paragraph Let I_n = Ker(R_n to R_1), base-ring calculation

proof.text: Use the specified cartesian identifications to regard $X_1\hookrightarrow X_n$ as first order thickenings over $\operatorname{Spec}R_1\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Spec}R_n$. Indeed, on an affine scheme chart the base change is the quotient of its coordinate ring $C$ by $I_n C$: this ideal has square zero, and every prime contains it. This verifies both the closed immersion and the full underlying closed subset directly. By [lem-sfb-space-first-order-ringed-description], all structure sheaves can be viewed on $X_{1,\mathrm{et}}$. Put $\mathcal E_n=\mathcal O_{X_n}$ on this site and $\mathcal F_n=\mathcal O_{X_1}\otimes_{R_1}I_n$. By the forward direction of [lem-sfb-space-square-zero-flatness-criterion], flatness of $X_n/R_n$ and the cartesian square identify the ideal of $X_1$ with $\mathcal F_n$. Consequently $0\to\mathcal F_n\to\mathcal E_n\to\mathcal O_{X_1}\to0$ is an extension of ring sheaves with square-zero kernel. The ideal identifications are canonical, so the transition maps on the kernels are $1\otimes(I_m\to I_n)$. The sheaf tensor definition [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] and the local-presentation definition [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module] show that these kernels are quasi-coherent: tensor a free-module presentation of $I_n$ with $\mathcal O_{X_1}$ to obtain its local presentation. Transition maps are surjective since each local tensor sum $\sum a_j\otimes i_j$ lifts by lifting its finitely many $i_j$.

source.place: Tag 0D3X (lemma-spaces-defo-thy), proof, displayed structure-sheaf extension, using Tag 06BH

proof.text: Form the sectionwise limits $\mathcal E=\varprojlim\mathcal E_n$ and $\mathcal G=\varprojlim\mathcal F_n$; componentwise operations preserve the sheaf gluing axiom. Then $0\to\mathcal G\to\mathcal E\to\mathcal O_{X_1}\to0$ is exact. Here is the local surjectivity argument, rather than an assumption that inverse limits preserve epimorphisms. On an affine etale object $U$ of $X_1$, [lem-sfb-space-surjective-qcoh-limit] gives $H^1(U,\mathcal F_n)=0$ and surjections $\mathcal F_{n+1}(U)\to\mathcal F_n(U)$. Hence each $\mathcal E_n(U)\to\mathcal O_{X_1}(U)$ is onto. Starting with a lift $e_n$ of $s$, choose any lift $e_{n+1}^0$ of $s$. Its image minus $e_n$ lies in $\mathcal F_n(U)$; lift that difference to $\mathcal F_{n+1}(U)$ and subtract it from $e_{n+1}^0$. Recursion gives a compatible lift of $s$. Kernel exactness holds coordinatewise. Products of elements of $\mathcal G$ vanish in every $\mathcal E_n$, so $\mathcal G$ is a square-zero ideal. The compatible base maps make this a ring-sheaf extension over $R\to R_1$.

source.place: Tag 0D3X (lemma-spaces-defo-thy), proof, inverse-limit extension and vanishing of R^1 lim of the kernels

proof.text: Set $\mathcal F=\mathcal O_{X_1}\otimes_{R_1}I$ and let $u:\mathcal F\to\mathcal G$ be the canonical map with components $1\otimes(I\to I_n)$. As in step 2, a free presentation of the module $I$ gives a local presentation of $\mathcal F$, so it is quasi-coherent. Apply [lem-sfb-proper-flat-space-pullback-limit] to $X_1\to\operatorname{Spec}R_1$ and the surjective tower $(I_n)$: the family is proper, flat and finitely presented by hypothesis. It gives, for every complex $K$ with quasi-coherent cohomology on $X_1$, a bijection $\operatorname{Hom}(K,\mathcal F[0])\to\operatorname{Hom}(K,\mathcal G[0])$ in the derived category. We use this derived testing statement; we do not identify the two ordinary module sheaves.

source.place: Tag 0D3X (lemma-spaces-defo-thy), proof, canonical tensor-to-limit map and Tag 0D3F

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-space-square-zero-extension-transfer] with $Z=X_1$, $B=\operatorname{Spec}R_1$, $B\prime=\operatorname{Spec}R$, $\mathcal F\to\mathcal G=u$, and base-ideal map $c:i\mapsto1\otimes i$. The space $X_1$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated because it is finitely presented over an affine base. Step 4 supplies exactly the universal derived-Hom hypothesis. In the extension $\mathcal E$ from step 3, the base ideal acts by $uc$: its nth component is the canonical ideal map $i_n\mapsto1\otimes i_n$. Essential surjectivity therefore supplies an extension $0\to\mathcal F\to\mathcal E\prime\to\mathcal O_{X_1}\to0$ over $R\to R_1$, together with an isomorphism from its pushout along $u$ to $\mathcal E$. In particular there is an $R$-algebra map $\mathcal E\prime\to\mathcal E$ inducing the identity on the quotient and $u$ on the kernels.

source.place: Tag 0D3X (lemma-spaces-defo-thy), proof, unique extension via the equivalence of Tag 0D3Q

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-space-first-order-ringed-description], the extension $\mathcal E\prime$, whose ideal $\mathcal F$ is quasi-coherent and square zero, is realized by a first order thickening $X_1\hookrightarrow X$ over $\operatorname{Spec}R$ with ring sheaf $\mathcal E\prime$. The induced base-ideal map $\mathcal O_{X_1}\otimes_{R_1}I\to\mathcal F$ is the identity by its prescribed value $c$. Apply the reverse direction of [lem-sfb-space-square-zero-flatness-criterion]: its reduced map $X_1\to\operatorname{Spec}R_1$ is flat. It follows that $X\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ is flat and that its reduction is cartesian, $X\times_R R_1\cong X_1$.

source.place: Tag 0D3X (lemma-spaces-defo-thy), proof, realization by Tag 05ZT and flatness by Tag 06BH

proof.text: For each $n$ the map $\mathcal E\prime\to\mathcal E\to\mathcal E_n$ induces, by the unique-morphism clause of [lem-sfb-space-first-order-ringed-description], a morphism $X_n\to X$ over $R$ reducing to the identity on $X_1$. Together with $X_n\to\operatorname{Spec}R_n$ it gives $h_n:X_n\to X\times_R R_n$ by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Its reduction over $R_n\to R_1$ is the identity: the target reduces to $(X\times_R R_n)\times_{R_n}R_1\cong X\times_R R_1\cong X_1$. The first identification is the unique one preserving the projections by the cited fibre-product universal property, and the second is step 6. The source reduces to $X_1$ by the specified cartesian data, and the reduced ring map is the identity on $\mathcal O_{X_1}$. Both reductions are first order thickenings, by the square-zero quotient calculation of step 2 applied to $R_n\to R_1$. Apply the isomorphism clause of [lem-sfb-space-flat-deformation-properties] over $\operatorname{Spec}R_1\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Spec}R_n$. Its source $X_n$ is flat over $R_n$ by hypothesis; the lemma imposes no flatness condition on its target. Thus $h_n$ is an isomorphism. For $m\ge n$, let $t_{nm}:X_n\to X_m$ be the morphism determined by the specified cartesian identification. The maps $X_n\to X$ and $X_n\xrightarrow{t_{nm}}X_m\to X$ induce the same ring map $\mathcal E\prime\to\mathcal E_n$, because the limit projections commute with the transition maps. The uniqueness clause gives equality of these morphisms. The fibre-product universal property now gives compatibility of all $h_n^{-1}:X\times_R R_n\cong X_n$ with every specified transition isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 0D3X (lemma-spaces-defo-thy), proof, base-change identification, making compatibility with the prescribed family explicit

proof.text: Finally apply [lem-sfb-space-flat-deformation-properties] to the structural morphism $X\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ with base thickening $\operatorname{Spec}R_1\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Spec}R$ and target the base itself. Step 6 gives both flatness of the source over $R$ and its cartesian reduction $X_1$. Since $X_1\to\operatorname{Spec}R_1$ is proper and finitely presented, the properness and finite-presentation clauses imply that $X\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ has these properties. Together with steps 6 and 7, this is the required family and all its compatible isomorphisms.

lean.note: The cartesian transition functor encodes the specified base-change isomorphisms and their identity/cocycle conditions.
